plain_english_revision: This amendment creates a specific exception to the standard six-year statute of limitations for civil lawsuits involving sex offenses against minors. Under current law, victims generally have until age 19 plus six years (age 25) to file suit. This bill allows individuals who were under 18 at the time an offense occurred to sue immediately if they are filing a claim in bankruptcy proceedings initiated on February 18, 2020, specifically against the estate of a congressionally chartered organization.
candidate_position_supported: The amendment supports expanding access to civil justice for survivors of sex offenses by removing time-barred limitations when suing specific types of organizations (congressionally chartered entities) in bankruptcy court. It affirms the policy that victims should not be permanently barred from seeking redress due to procedural timelines if they are pursuing claims against a bankrupt organization's estate.
evidence_quotes: This bill would provide an exception to the statute of limitations for a civil action for injury resulting from certain sex offenses against a minor, provided the action is for purposes of making a claim against the bankruptcy estate...
